label: Limited Test Ban Treaty
short_note: Signed Aug 5, 1963; in force Oct 10, 1963. Bans nuclear tests in outer space. It followed Starfish Prime; fallout concerns and the Cuban Missile Crisis were also drivers.
citation: Treaty Banning Nuclear Weapon Tests in the Atmosphere, in Outer Space and Under Water, Aug. 5, 1963, 14 U.S.T. 1313, 480 U.N.T.S. 43.

label: Outer Space Treaty
short_note: Opened Jan 27, 1967; in force Oct 10, 1967. Art. IV bars nuclear weapons and WMD in orbit; silent on conventional ASATs.
citation: Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, Jan. 27, 1967, 18 U.S.T. 2410, 610 U.N.T.S. 205.

label: ABM Treaty Art. XII
short_note: Bars interference with the other party's 'national technical means' of verification (bilateral; US withdrew 2002).
citation: Treaty on the Limitation of Anti-Ballistic Missile Systems, U.S.-U.S.S.R., art. XII, May 26, 1972, 23 U.S.T. 3435.

label: PAROS (UNGA agenda item)
short_note: First PAROS resolutions adopted Dec 9, 1981 (UNGA 36/97 C; 36/99). CD Ad Hoc Committee on PAROS met 1985-94. No treaty has resulted.

label: CD Ad Hoc Committee on PAROS
short_note: Conference on Disarmament committee re-established annually 1985-1994; mandate lapsed.
citation: Conference on Disarmament, Ad Hoc Committee on the Prevention of an Arms Race in Outer Space (1985-1994).

label: ITU Constitution Arts. 45 & 48
short_note: Adopted Geneva 1992; in force July 1, 1994. Art. 45 prohibits harmful interference; Art. 48 gives military radio installations 'complete freedom' (the core gap for jamming). The Radio Regulations sit beneath the Constitution.
citation: Constitution of the International Telecommunication Union arts. 45, 48, Dec. 22, 1992, 1825 U.N.T.S. 331.

label: PPWT draft (Russia-China)
short_note: Draft treaty on preventing placement of weapons in outer space, tabled at the CD. Does not cover ground-based (direct-ascent) ASATs.
citation: Draft Treaty on the Prevention of the Placement of Weapons in Outer Space, CD/1839 (Feb. 29, 2008).

label: PPWT updated draft
short_note: Revised draft; still silent on ground-based ASATs and testing.

label: Tallinn Manual 2.0 (soft law)
short_note: Expert manual on international law applicable to cyber operations. Not binding law.
citation: Tallinn Manual 2.0 on the International Law Applicable to Cyber Operations (Michael N. Schmitt ed., Cambridge Univ. Press 2017).

label: UNGA 75/36
short_note: Reducing space threats through norms, rules and principles of responsible behaviour.

label: McGill (MILAMOS) Manual Vol. I (soft law)
short_note: Expert manual on international law applicable to military uses of outer space. Not binding law.
citation: McGill Manual on International Law Applicable to Military Uses of Outer Space, Vol. I - Rules (Ram S. Jakhu & Steven Freeland eds., McGill Centre for Research in Air & Space Law 2022).

label: US DA-ASAT test moratorium
short_note: US commits not to conduct destructive direct-ascent ASAT missile tests. Followed by Canada, New Zealand, Japan, Germany, UK, France and others; SWF counts 38 states in total.
citation: The White House, Fact Sheet: Vice President Harris Advances National Security Norms in Space (Apr. 18, 2022); SWF 2026, p. 01-50.

label: OEWG on space threats
short_note: Open-ended working group under Res. 76/231; ended without a consensus report.

label: UNGA 77/41 (DA-ASAT tests)
short_note: Calls on states to commit not to conduct destructive direct-ascent ASAT missile tests. Adopted 155-9-9.

label: Woomera Manual (soft law)
short_note: Expert manual on international law of military space operations. Not binding law.
citation: The Woomera Manual on the International Law of Military Space Activities and Operations (Jack Beard et al. eds., Oxford Univ. Press 2024).

label: Russian veto: nuclear weapons in orbit
short_note: Russia vetoed a US-Japan draft reaffirming OST Art. IV (no nuclear weapons in orbit). Vote 13-1-1 (China abstained). The draft did not concern DA-ASAT testing.
citation: U.N. SCOR, 79th Sess., 9616th mtg., U.N. Doc. S/PV.9616 (Apr. 24, 2024); draft S/2024/302.

label: ITU RRB: 'grave concern' (Sweden, France)
short_note: Radio Regulations Board expressed grave concern about intentional harmful interference to Swedish and French satellites that seemed to originate from earth stations in Russia.
citation: ITU Radio Regulations Board, 96th meeting (July 2024), summary of decisions; SWF 2026, p. 02-32.

label: ICAO: Russia's GNSS interference breaches Chicago Convention
short_note: ICAO found GNSS interference originating in Russia infringed the 1944 Chicago Convention, condemned it, and called on Russia to meet its obligations.
citation: ICAO action on GNSS radio frequency interference (Oct. 2025), as reported in SWF 2026, p. 02-30.

label: ITU RRB 100th meeting: urges Russia to cease RNSS interference
short_note: Board again urged Russia to immediately cease harmful interference to radionavigation-satellite service receivers in Estonia, Finland, Latvia and Lithuania.
citation: ITU Radio Regulations Board, 100th meeting (Nov. 2025); SWF 2026, p. 02-30.
